brewing.notes: A common starting point for herbal infusions: boiling water, about five minutes.

description:
A ready-to-drink herbal cooling tea from Guiding County, Guizhou, extracted from plants of the Yunwu Mountain area and based on Miao and Buyi recipes. Its sweetness comes from a sweet herb rather than cane sugar.

Brew it as you would other herbal infusions. If the plant is new to you, check that it is safe for you first, especially when pregnant or on medication.
name_ru: Гуй Дин И Гань Цао Лян Ча
history: Said to go back to the late Qing, it began as a folk thirst-quenching brew among the Buyi and Miao, with a Buyi healer family named Zhao credited in local accounts. Before 1949 it was made in household workshops and was known across central Guizhou. It received national geographical indication protection on 10 August 2015, covering 20 townships of the county.
processing: Plant extract is obtained by an extraction process and bottled, without cane sugar or other additives.
harvest_season: Depends on the plant and the place.
appearance_liquor: Depends on the plant; usually pale to amber.
taste_profile: Clean herbal taste with a sweet aftertaste that is not cloying.
vintage_note: Herbal infusions are not sold by vintage: buy recent stock and use it within a year or so.
